title: Fossils and Geologic Time
seo_title: Grade 7 Science: Fossils and Geologic Time Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Earth and its climate have changed over geological time: the fossil record, relative dating of rock layers, and the geologic time scale. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 7, Earth and Space Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 science worksheets (BC): how fossils form, rock layers and relative age, index fossils, and the geologic time scale. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Fossils show how life on Earth has changed.
key_sub: Lower rock layers are usually older.
body_html:
How to think about it

Fossils form when remains or traces of living things are buried in sediment and turn to rock. In undisturbed rock layers, the lowest layer is the oldest (the law of superposition).

The geologic time scale divides Earth's 4.6 billion years into eons, eras and periods. Humans appeared only a very short time ago. BC has famous fossil sites such as the Burgess Shale in Yoho National Park.

Example

Which rock layer is oldest if the layers have not been disturbed?

Layers pile up over time.

Answer: the bottom layer

Example

Which kind of rock usually contains fossils?

It forms in layers.

Answer: sedimentary

Common mistakes

  • Thinking fossils form in lava (igneous rock).
  • Thinking dinosaurs and humans lived at the same time.
  • Thinking the top layer is always the oldest.

items.q: Benjamin observes in a cliff: “A worn, uneven surface (an unconformity) lies between two sets of layers.” What can be concluded?
c: The two layers formed at about the same time (an index fossil).
The tilted layers formed and were tilted before the flat layers were deposited.
Some rock was eroded away, so part of the record is missing.
The granite is older than the sandstone.
items.e: Relative dating uses superposition, cross-cutting features, unconformities, inclusions and index fossils.
